moveDecisions.rationale: The opening clearly states the motion position and announces a positive evidentiary case, supporting the stronger constructive-opening responsiveness candidate.

The move states a clear distinction, but the categorical claim that legendary molding has no bearing is insufficiently qualified and somewhat stronger than the examples warrant; it does not substantially represent a live alternative.

The passage asserts independence, early dating, and Palestinian origin without representing an alternative view; its source scope is incompletely specified and its strong probability language lacks an explicit caveat.

The proposition is recoverable and terminologically stable, but the broad description of what mythicists often say weakens their position; the certainty of the Pauline interpretation remains somewhat underqualified.

The passage moves categorically from Paul's wording to knowing Jesus's biological brother and closest disciple, although the interpretive bridge concerning 'brother of the Lord' remains contested and implicit.
The move advances a probability argument from the counterexpectational crucified-Messiah claim, and it does not sufficiently develop a live alternative for charity to be tested.

The move directly challenges the independent force of calling traditions early, but supplies limited warrant, reaches only the subsidiary probabilistic-method bridge, caricatures the opposing chronology as circular, and leaves its own scope partly unstable.

The move squarely presses whether removing legendary attributes leaves an independently explanatory person, but the Superman analogy weakens the opposing distinction; the proposition remains recoverable despite a partly unstable comparison.

The inference from dependence on circulating oral tradition to limited independent attestation is coherent and directly targeted, though labeling the material simply as hearsay compresses distinctions and leaves terms partly unstable.

The Josephus discussion is relevant contrary material but does not contact the broader multiple-source claim; its proposition and qualification are explicit, while its probabilistic conclusion appropriately acknowledges textual uncertainty.
The move directly contests whether the asserted source strata are actual independent witnesses rather than contested reconstructions, making the first full-answer candidate the better fit.

The move directly frames the earthly-versus-celestial interpretation of Paul's rulers and gives the opposing reading recognizable contact, but its Gnostic parallel only slightly supports the proposed Pauline interpretation.

The passage accurately identifies the live issue as historical transmission versus revelation and expressly concedes uncertainty, but candidate one better reflects its fair yet still adversarial representation.

The move directly addresses whether hostile ancient testimony presupposed an earthly Jesus; its terms and scope are stable, although the evidentiary force is presented somewhat more strongly than the dependence question permits.

The move answers the methodological challenge by distinguishing critical recovery from naïve demythologizing and treats the objection fairly, but offers only compressed methodological support and leaves key recovery criteria partly unspecified.

The chronology objection directly attacks the central celestial-origin bridge, but it slides from late surviving texts toward a stronger claim about antecedent ideas, leaving scope and necessity insufficiently qualified.

The causal thesis is internally intelligible and answers the demythologized-core issue, but it gives limited evidence for necessity, understates alternative origin mechanisms, and leaves the scope and qualifications materially incomplete.

The move supplies a pre-Pauline Israelite alternative to the Gnostic background, but its compressed sequence of analogies and divine-name claims makes important terms less stable than the higher precision candidate allows.

The move questions whether an ordinary executed teacher adequately explains Christianity and explicitly concedes possibility; the Superman framing weakens the opponent, while the cautious force is well matched to the warrant.

The hermeneutical-circle discussion bears on critical recovery rather than directly answering bare existence; its terminology is partly unstable, but its plausibility-level conclusion and acknowledgment of revision are calibrated.

The Caesar comparison explicitly defeats the inference from false supernatural claims to nonexistence and accurately contacts both live objections; the central proposition, scope, and qualification are fully recoverable.

The move engages both bare compatibility and explanatory significance, though its commonplace-founder analogy weakens the opposing account; candidate one best captures this limited but not gross representational defect.

The move directly challenges the reliability and recoverability of Gospel historical anchors, but the conclusion that Jesus becomes freely insertable is materially stronger than the listed defects alone establish.

The move reframes the dispute around comparative historical probability, addressing rival paradigms, defective anchors, and hearsay while directly supporting the pro motion-level historical-person bridge.
